To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following four main steps are needed to select an outcome measurement instrument: 1) conceptual considerations, 2) finding existing outcome measurement instrument, 3) quality assessment, and 4) generic recommendations on the final selection of the outcome measurement instrument for the core outcome.
COS developers can follow the four steps of our COSMIN-based guideline for the selection of outcome instruments.

the selection of outcome instruments for COS is best achieved by a systematic and transparent process, including four main steps, namely conceptual considerations, finding existing instruments, quality assessment of instruments, and generic recommendations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selection of outcome instruments, whereas other COS developers focus on the selection of outcomes.
the selection of outcome measures, not with the development of new outcome measures, which is the topic of another guideline.
the selection of outcome instruments for the outcomes that are to be included in a COS, and not with the development of a COS itself, which is the focus of the COMET initiative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the COS developers need to: 1) consider conceptual considerations, such as the definition of the outcome of interest, and the selection of the most important outcomes to be included in the COS; 2) search for existing outcome measurement instruments by means of systematic reviews and/or literature searches, and consider whether to include a new outcome measurement instrument; 3) assess the quality of the existing outcome measurement instruments; 4) consider generic recommendations on the final selection of outcome measurement instrument(s).

COS developers should select outcome measurement instruments based on the following steps: 1) Conceptual considerations, 2) Finding existing outcome measurement instruments by means of a literature search, 3) Quality assessment of outcome measurement instrument, and 4) Recommendations on the selection of an outcome measurement instrument.

a COS developer should first define the conceptual considerations of the outcomes, second search for existing outcome measurement instruments for the outcomes, third assess the measurement properties and other feasibility aspects of the outcome measurement instruments, and finally select outcome measurement instruments based on the results of the assessment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COS developers should select outcome measurement instruments based on the conceptual considerations, feasibility aspects, and measurement properties of the outcome measurement instruments.
the selection of outcome instruments should be guided by a systematic and transparent process.

COS developers should start their search for measurement instruments by performing a systematic review of measurement instruments, followed by a systematic review of their psychometric properties and feasibility aspects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a COS should be based on a comprehensive search strategy, and should include a quality assessment of outcome measurements.
COS developers should be very explicit in defining the outcomes of interest and in selecting the most appropriate outcome measurement instruments.
the selection of outcome instruments is a multi-faceted process that involves both methodological and practical considerations, and requires input from different stakeholders.
